title: Specified point-transport cone comparison and descent through roofs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_n(x)=x\otimes1$, and $t_n=1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$, with the coefficient-induced transition $v_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b); put $D_n=\Gamma P_n$, $B_n=\Gamma C_n$. All these towers are over the single integral coefficient ring after restriction of scalars. For a strict tower $X_\bullet$ with transitions $w_n$ set $s_X((x_n)_n)=(w_nx_{n+1})_n$ and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$, with $H(X)^i=\prod_nX_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^i$ and $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Let $N$ be a complex of $R$-modules and $q:P\to N$ a quasi-isomorphism. Use $\sigma$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] and $\theta_n=\kappa_{P_n}g^{-1}(r_n)$ of comparison (b) [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Suppose $u:D_\bullet\to B_\bullet$ is a strict tower map satisfying $\Gamma(\theta_n)\sigma_P=u_n\Gamma(r_n)$ for every $n$. Put $a_P(z)=(0,(\Gamma(r_n)z)_n)$ and $\widetilde\theta_P(w)=(0,(\theta_nw)_n)$; let $c_C:\Gamma H(C_\bullet)\to H(B_\bullet)$ be the identity on the two sectionwise product components. Then the following is a chain-map equality, including the shifted-product component:
$$c_C\Gamma(\widetilde\theta_P)\sigma_P=H(u)a_P.$$
Use the ambient completed pullback $Lg^*$ on $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], whose restriction to integral constructible objects is [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Under its specified representative comparison identifying $Lg^*N$ with $H(C_\bullet)$, let $b_q:\Gamma Lg^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}H(B_\bullet)$ be induced by $c_C$. The specified integral comparison $\kappa_N=[\widetilde\theta_P][g^{-1}q]^{-1}$ and $\iota_N=\Gamma(\kappa_N)\sigma_N$ satisfy
$$b_q\iota_N\Gamma(q)=[H(u)a_P],\qquad b_q\iota_N=[H(u)a_P][\Gamma(q)]^{-1}.$$
Here exact sections make $\Gamma(q)$ invertible, and $\sigma_N\Gamma(q)=\Gamma(g^{-1}q)\sigma_P$. These identities compare the actual integral map of part (b), including its zero shifted-product component. If the family $u(P)$ commutes with chain maps between flat-term K-flat representatives, these identities are independent of those representatives under the specified completed-pullback comparison maps and are natural for arbitrary derived morphisms: for any roof $P\xleftarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{b}P'$ with $a$ a quasi-isomorphism in that resolving class they commute with $[b][a]^{-1}$. No derived-completeness hypothesis on $[N]$ and no invertibility of $[a_P][\Gamma(q)]^{-1}$ is required.

proof.text: Write $r=(r_n)_n$ and $\theta=(\theta_n)_n$. The reductions satisfy $t_nr_{n+1}=r_n$: on a tensor generator this says that reducing $x\otimes1$ once more gives $x\otimes1$. Part (b) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] gives $v_n\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n$ and that every $\theta_n$ is a chain map over the completed coefficient sheaf. Thus $(1-s_D)\Gamma(r)=0$ and $(1-s_C)\theta=0$. With the displayed differential, $d(0,\theta(w))=(0,\theta(dw))$ and $d(0,\Gamma(r)z)=(0,\Gamma(r)dz)$. Consequently both specified zero-first-component lifts are chain maps; this uses equality in the strict towers before localization.

source.place: clause (3), explicit strict-cone comparison and localization calculation written by Q121

proof.text: For a strict tower map $f:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$ define $U_f((x_n))=(f_nx_n)$. Strictness gives $(1-s_Y)U_f=U_f(1-s_X)$, so $H(f)(b,a)=(U_fb,U_fa)$ commutes with $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$. In particular this specifies $H(u)$ on both products. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], evaluation of the sheaf products is the product of the evaluations. Sections are additive and exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], so they identify the finite direct sum and both differentials as well. Hence $c_C$ is a chain isomorphism, identity on the two products, and for every strict map of sheaf towers $f$ it satisfies $c_{C'}\Gamma H(f)=H(\Gamma f)c_C$.

source.place: clause (3), explicit strict-cone comparison and localization calculation written by Q121

proof.text: Evaluate the left side of the claimed strict equality on $z\in\Gamma(P)^i$. By the definitions of the lifts and of $c_C$, it is $(0,(\Gamma(\theta_n)\sigma_Pz)_n)$. The assumed augmentation equations identify this with $(0,(u_n\Gamma(r_n)z)_n)$. The diagonal formula in step 2 identifies the latter with $H(u)a_P(z)$. The first product component in degree $i-1$ is zero on both sides, not merely invisible under projection to a finite level. Equality degree by degree proves the asserted equality of chain maps.

source.place: clause (3), explicit strict-cone comparison and localization calculation written by Q121

proof.text: Clause (1) of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] applies to every complex of integral coefficient modules, without constructibility or completeness. For the chain map $q:P\to N$ it gives $\sigma_N\Gamma(q)=\Gamma(g^{-1}q)\sigma_P$. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], $\Gamma(q)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The transported module inverse image in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so $\Gamma(g^{-1}q)$ is one too. Their classes are therefore invertible in the derived category.

source.place: clause (3), explicit strict-cone comparison and localization calculation written by Q121

proof.text:
The ambient operation of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] is represented on $q:P\to N$ by $H(C_\bullet)$. Its functorial representative comparisons and their independence are supplied by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined](2). Composing that comparison with $c_C$ defines the asserted $b_q$. Under it, part (b) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] gives $\Gamma(\kappa_N)=[\Gamma\widetilde\theta_P][\Gamma(g^{-1}q)]^{-1}$. Combine this formula with step 4 and then step 3:
$$b_q\iota_N[\Gamma(q)]=[c_C\Gamma\widetilde\theta_P][\Gamma(g^{-1}q)]^{-1}\sigma_N[\Gamma(q)]=[c_C\Gamma\widetilde\theta_P]\sigma_P=[H(u)a_P].$$
Right-compose with $[\Gamma(q)]^{-1}$ for the second displayed identity. At this point only the resolution maps and $c_C$ have been inverted.

source.place: clause (3), explicit strict-cone comparison and localization calculation written by Q121

proof.text: Assume now the stated chain naturality of $u(P)$. For a chain map $h:P\to P'$ in the resolving class write $h_D,h_B,h_C$ for its induced tower maps. Reduction gives $\Gamma(h_n)\Gamma(r_n)=\Gamma(r'_n)\Gamma(h)$, since both maps send $x$ to $h(x)\otimes1$. Similarly, the finite comparison $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](a) gives $h_{C,n}\theta_n=\theta'_ng^{-1}h$. Thus $H(h_D)a_P=a_{P'}\Gamma(h)$, and $H(h_C)\widetilde\theta_P=\widetilde\theta_{P'}g^{-1}h$, including zero first components. By the assumption $h_Bu(P)=u(P')h_D$ and the diagonal formula, putting $\eta_P=[H(u(P))a_P]$ gives $[H(h_B)]\eta_P=\eta_{P'}[\Gamma(h)]$. The maps $c_C$ commute with these comparisons by step 2.

source.place: clause (3), explicit strict-cone comparison and localization calculation written by Q121

proof.text: Use the small-site and module-universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], localization of the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat module complexes at its quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to the ambient $D(R)$. The source functor on this class is $P\mapsto\Gamma P$; its homotopy and quasi-isomorphism invariance follows from exact sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. The target functor is $P\mapsto\Gamma H(C(P))$, identified with $H(B(P))$ by $c_C$. Its factorization through the derived category, quasi-isomorphism invariance and specified natural representative comparisons are exactly [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined](1),(2), followed by exact sections. Therefore the chain naturality equations of step 6 are also equations in the homotopy category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2),(3), with these two functors and the resolving-class localization, to extend $\eta$ uniquely to a natural transformation of the ambient derived functors. This uses the equivalence for all flat-term K-flat objects, rather than assuming a chain lift between two arbitrarily chosen resolutions.

source.place: clause (3), explicit strict-cone comparison and localization calculation written by Q121

proof.text:
Explicitly, for the stated roof put $S(h)=[\Gamma(h)]$ and $T(h)=[H(h_B)]$. Both $S(a)$ and $T(a)$ are invertible by step 7. Naturality for $a:Q\to P$ gives $T(a)^{-1}\eta_P=\eta_QS(a)^{-1}$. Hence
$$T(b)T(a)^{-1}\eta_P=T(b)\eta_QS(a)^{-1}=\eta_{P'}S(b)S(a)^{-1}.$$
This is the required square for $[b][a]^{-1}$, and step 7 ensures independence of its presentation. For a representative $q:P\to N$, the descended component, expressed using $b_q$, is $\eta_P[\Gamma(q)]^{-1}$ by naturality. Step 5 identifies this with the specified $\iota_N$. Uniqueness of the descent and the specified target comparisons then identify the expressions from any two representatives. The strict equality in step 3 and its derived versions therefore describe the same natural map. No step inverted $a_P$ or invoked completeness of $N$.

tool_uses.why: Sectionwise products identify both coordinates of the strict Roos cone; the unit has no such general sheaf-product theorem.
Exact point sections invert the resolution quasi-isomorphisms; no constructibility is required.
Uses invariance under good quasi-isomorphisms and the specified natural comparisons for ambient completed pullback, not a different purity route.
Only its resolving-class localization equivalence is used for arbitrary derived morphisms; the unit does not supply that generic localization theorem.
Only clause (1), ambient chain naturality of sigma, is used; no naturality of integral iota is presumed.
